questions.title: Parse a strict port configuration
questions.prompt: Accept a nonempty string containing ASCII digits only and a number in 1..65535. Leading zeroes are allowed. Reject spaces, signs, trailing text, zero, and out-of-range numbers with std::invalid_argument.

tests.label: Leading zeros
tests.hint: Accumulate digits instead of rejecting leading zeros.

tests.label: Above range
tests.hint: Reject a value as soon as it exceeds the limit.

tests.label: Zero and empty
tests.hint: Reject both zero and an empty input.

hints: Check each character before turning it into a digit.
Checking the 65535 bound after every digit keeps the next int multiplication small.
questions.explanation: The loop validates the entire representation. Incremental range checks prevent accumulation from reaching int overflow. The rules are explicit rather than relying on a parser that accepts prefixes.

questions.title: Return the largest k measurements
questions.prompt: Return up to k values in descending order. Keep duplicate values. Do not change the input. If k exceeds the input size, return all values. Tests check results, not performance.
questions.signature: std::vector<int> topK(const std::vector<int>& values, std::size_t k)

tests.label: Keep duplicates
tests.hint: Duplicate measurements occupy separate result slots.

tests.label: Larger than input
tests.hint: Clamp k to the input size.

tests.label: Negative values
tests.hint: Descending order still applies to negative numbers.

hints: Copy the input before rearranging it.
partial_sort can order just the requested prefix; a full sort is also correct but may do more work.
questions.explanation: partial_sort places the largest k values at the front when used with greater<int>. Resizing removes the unused suffix. Tests validate behavior; benchmarking is a separate task.

questions.title: Count adjacent runs without extra storage
questions.prompt: A run is a consecutive group of equal values. Return the number of runs. The values 1,1,2,1 contain three runs. Empty input has zero. Use a single pass; tests check answers rather than allocation behavior.

tests.label: One run
tests.hint: Equal neighbors stay in the same run.

tests.label: Empty
tests.hint: Handle empty input before starting at one.

tests.label: Every item differs
tests.hint: Each changed neighbor starts a new run.

hints: A nonempty vector starts with one run.
Each later item starts a new run only when it differs from its predecessor.
questions.explanation: Only the previous element matters. No auxiliary container is required, so this is a useful example of keeping a scan simple.
